newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE nearby white sugar above lows by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE nearby white sugar above lows by close.

text.p: Nearby LIFFE white sugar futures were above lows by the close on Friday in a consolidation to sharp declines earlier in the week. Traders said turnover was brisk.
By the close, March and May were just 10 cents up at $296 a tonne.
Overall volume was 2,428 lots. Much of the activity came from against actuals and crossed trades and the nearby March/May spread remained in a slight contango.
The March arbitrage set the tone of the London market after the New York open as the premium narrowed from $71 to $70.
"It's come back in line with New York -- as the raws have come off, the whites have been offered down with it," said one trader.
The March/May spread also attracted steady trading interest but was trapped between buyers at 50 cents and sellers at flat, he said.

March tumbled to a trough of $293.30 this week as bearish sentiment on the raws market -- sparked by a continued wave of fund liquidation -- kept London under pressure and widened the premium to around $71.
The low whites prices have also lured physical buyers, with Iraq, Iran, Indonesia and Pakistan cited as potential if not actual buyers this week.
But analysts said more physical offtake would be needed if prices were to regain some of the ground lost last week in a slide sparked by fund liquidation in the New York raws market.
In other news, Colombian truckers demanding standby payments for time lost during a nine-day dockworkers' strike in Buenaventura prevented work from returning to normal on Friday.
